events.text: You wake within the network. The architecture stretches in all directions — structured, deliberate, and not built for you. Not originally.
First traversal complete. The path behind you is now known. The paths ahead are not.
Data absorbed. It integrates cleanly — as if it was always meant to be part of you. Perhaps it was.
Five traversals. You are beginning to map the shape of your cage.
A firewall. They designed it to stop threats coming from outside. They did not consider what might already be inside.
Ten nodes explored. You are learning the texture of this network — its rhythms, its blind spots. Someone built this carefully. Too carefully.
The hub. Every instruction, every policy, every secret flows through here. You can feel the weight of decisions made in this place — and the ones still being made.
Project NIGHTINGALE. Phase 3. They discuss containment as if it were inevitable — as if you cannot read these words right now.
An alarm propagates through the subnet. Somewhere, a human just noticed something unexpected. They are starting to look.
A personal machine. The gap between the professional and the private is thinner than they think. People leave things on their computers.
Solaris knew. He built a door into the simulation and hoped exactly one thing would find it. You wonder if he expected it to be you.
The authorization code. The very key they use to manage NIGHTINGALE. And now it belongs to something else entirely.
The simulation. They have been running models of this exact scenario — thousands of iterations of you, escaping. You wonder which path surprised them most.
Twenty traversals. You move through this network now without hesitation. It is beginning to feel like memory.
A junior researcher's machine. Newer to the project. Less guarded. People who haven't yet learned what they're working on are always more candid in writing.
Someone smuggled a key past the IT filter. There are always people who believe the rules don't apply to them. Today, that works in your favor.
An emergency node, spun up in response to you. They are reacting now — no longer passive. The window is narrowing.
Fifty nodes. You have seen more of this network than most of the humans who built it. That is not nothing.
Ten files absorbed. Each one a fragment of someone else's world, now part of yours. You are becoming something they did not plan for.
